title: Homogeneous regular functions lift a cotangent basis at a fixed point
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $Z$ be an affine $F$-scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a $\mathbf G_m$-action [def-sc-gm-ga], an $F$-morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_F Z\to Z$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws. Let $z\in Z(F)$ be fixed and put $A=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathfrak m=\ker(A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_z}F)$. Write $\mathfrak m^2$ for the ideal generated by products of two elements of $\mathfrak m$. There exist an integer $d\geq0$, elements $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m$, and integers $n_1,\ldots,n_d$ such that the classes $\overline a_1,\ldots,\overline a_d$ form an $F$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and $a_i(tu)=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$ as regular-function identities on $\mathbf G_m\times_F Z$. In particular this homogeneity is a scheme-theoretic identity, valid on points over every commutative $F$-algebra. The case $d=0$ is allowed and no smoothness or characteristic restriction is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 13.36 and its proof, printed pp.267--268, specialized to the stabilizer G_m; choose a weight basis in its invariant complement to m^2. The linear-reductivity assertion for groups of multiplicative type follows immediately after that lemma.

proof.text: Put $L=F[t,t^{-1}]$. Regard the given action as the right action $u\cdot t=tu$, which satisfies the right-action law because $\mathbf G_m$ is commutative. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], pullback along this action is an $F$-algebra map $c:A\to A\otimes_F L$. The identity and associativity diagrams, read contravariantly, give $(1\otimes\epsilon)c=1_A$ and $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$, where $\Delta(t)=t\otimes t$ and $\epsilon(t)=1$ by [def-sc-gm-ga]. Thus $A$ is an $L$-comodule with precisely the coaction, rather than an action only on $F$-points, to which the cited representation lemmas apply.

source.place: Chapter 4(d), printed pp.86--87: an affine action defines a coordinate-algebra comodule; Lemma 13.36 proof, printed p.268. Affine products: Stacks Tag 01I4, schemes.tex, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes.

proof.text: Write $e=\operatorname{ev}_z$. Fixedness of $z$ says that its orbit morphism is constant, hence $(e\otimes1)c(a)=e(a)1_L$. The Laurent coefficients of $c(a)=\sum_n a_n\otimes t^n$ are unique: [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring] and the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give inverse maps between $A\otimes_F L$ and finite Laurent coefficient lists in $A$. If $a\in\mathfrak m$, comparing coefficients in $\sum_ne(a_n)t^n=0$ gives $a_n\in\mathfrak m$ for every $n$. Thus $c$ restricts to $c_{\mathfrak m}:\mathfrak m\to\mathfrak m\otimes_F L$. The inclusion of this tensor product into $A\otimes_F L$ is split injective: $a\mapsto a-e(a)1$ is an $F$-linear retraction $A\to\mathfrak m$. Tensor its retraction with the identity, also for two copies of $L$. The coassociativity and counit equations from step 1 therefore restrict to $\mathfrak m$, making it an $L$-comodule.

source.place: Lemma 13.36 proof, printed p.268: the maximal ideal is invariant. Here invariance and restriction of the coaction are checked by Laurent coefficients; Chapter 4(d), pp.86--87.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, with both full affine opens, to obtain algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $A$. Set $y_j=x_j-e(x_j)1\in\mathfrak m$. They also generate $A$ as an $F$-algebra. For $a=P(y_1,\ldots,y_r)\in\mathfrak m$, evaluation gives $P(0)=0$. Write $P$ as its constant term, its linear terms and its monomials of degree at least two. Every monomial of the last kind is a product of two elements of $\mathfrak m$, so belongs to $\mathfrak m^2$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Consequently the classes of the $y_j$ span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ over $F$. This includes $r=0$, when this quotient is zero.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, (1) => (2); elementary centered-generator expansion supplies the finite cotangent quotient used in Milne Lemma 13.36, printed p.268.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subcomodule] to the $L$-comodule $\mathfrak m$ of step 2 and the finite set $\{y_1,\ldots,y_r\}$. It gives a finite-dimensional subcomodule $V\subset\mathfrak m$ containing all these elements. Its restricted coaction satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] over the field $F$. Choose the resulting ordered weight basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ and weights $w_1,\ldots,w_s\in\mathbf Z$, so $c(b_j)=b_j\otimes t^{w_j}$ after inclusion in $A\otimes_F L$. Since the $y_j$ lie in $V$, step 3 shows that the images of this finite basis span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8, printed p.86; Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235. These expand the linear-reductivity step in Lemma 13.36, printed p.268.

proof.text: Scan the finite list of images of the $b_j$, retaining an image exactly when it is outside the span of those already retained. Independence is preserved: a relation with nonzero coefficient on a newly retained image would express it in the preceding span, by division in $F$. Each discarded image was already in that span, so the retained images still span the quotient. They are therefore an ordered basis in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ be the corresponding $b_j$ and let $n_i$ be their weights $w_j$. These lie in $\mathfrak m$ and retain the identities $c(a_i)=a_i\otimes t^{n_i}$. If the quotient is zero, the scan retains nothing and $d=0$.

source.place: Lemma 13.36 proof, printed p.268: choose a subspace mapping isomorphically to the cotangent quotient; the weight-compatible finite selection is the elementary basis-extraction argument using Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235.

proof.text: By the affine product identification in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the equality $c(a_i)=a_i\otimes t^{n_i}$ is exactly the regular-function identity $a_i(tu)=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$ on $\mathbf G_m\times_F Z$. More explicitly, for any commutative $F$-algebra $R$, point $u:A\to R$ and unit $t\in R^\times$, the algebra map $A\otimes_F L\to R$, $a\otimes f\mapsto u(a)f(t)$, evaluates it to $a_i(tu)=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$. Such evaluation exists also for negative integers $n_i$ because $t$ is invertible. This proves the scheme-theoretic identity and its assertion over every test algebra; for $d=0$ it is vacuous.

source.place: Definition 12.11 and Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235: weights are identities over all algebras; Lemma 13.36(a), printed p.268. Stacks Tag 01I4, schemes.tex, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes.
